name: Sovereign Equity & Overage Recovery Engine
tag: Find, qualify and document unclaimed tax-sale and foreclosure surplus funds.

scenarios.title: Find surplus funds in one county
scenarios.ask: Show surplus funds from {sales} tax sales over the last {years} in one sample county, over {threshold}.
steps: Read {sales} sample tax-sale results from the last {years}.
{=round(sales * 0.61 / threshold)} sales left a surplus over {threshold} after the debt was paid.
Checked claim deadlines. {=round(round(sales * 0.61 / threshold) * min(0.95, 1.06 - years * 0.1))} are still open.
Prepared a claim packet checklist for each open case.

result.title: Sample county
rows: Sample data; rules differ by state

followups: Why do older sales have fewer open claims?

Many jurisdictions set a deadline to claim surplus funds, and some unclaimed money moves to the state or county. Looking back {years}, about {=round(min(0.95, 1.06 - years * 0.1) * 100)}% of sample cases are still open.
Usually the former owner or their heirs, and sometimes lienholders. Rules on third-party help and finder fees differ by state, so the engine records each jurisdiction's rules with every case.

scenarios.title: Qualify one lead
scenarios.ask: A sample property sold with a ${surplus} surplus. It has {liens} recorded liens. Is it worth pursuing?
steps: Pulled the sample sale record, surplus amount and recorded liens.
Estimated that {liens} junior liens may claim about ${=round(surplus * min(0.9, liens * 0.12))} first, depending on state rules.
Owner status: {owner}. Estimated {=owner * 3} weeks to reach the right claimant.
Scored the lead on net amount, deadline and paperwork load.
followups: Why do heir cases take longer?
Heirs often need probate or an affidavit of heirship before a claim is paid. The engine lists which documents the sample jurisdiction asks for.
Not always. Priority depends on state law and the type of lien. The estimate is a planning number until the claim is reviewed.

scenarios.title: Track the claims pipeline
scenarios.ask: We have {cases} open sample cases. Show where each one stands and what to do this week.

inputs.label: Days to flag before a deadline

steps: Sorted {cases} cases into found, contacted, signed, filed and paid.
Found {=max(1, round(cases * deadline / 600))} cases with a deadline in the next {deadline}.
Drafted mail-first contact letters for cases not yet reached.
followups: Does it file claims for us?
It prepares packets and checklists. A person reviews and files each claim, since signatures and notarization are required in many places.
Letter templates are set per state, and the engine records consent and contact history for each case. Have counsel review templates before use.
